newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Sept 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Sept 25.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Wednesday:
* The Federal Reserve Board's policymaking body adjourned its meeting Tuesday without changing a key short-term interest rate.
* Repulican presidential nominee Bob Dole criticized the Clinton Administration's handling of the U.S. economy, which Dole said was "not on the right track."
* President Clinton signed a treaty at the United Nations that would ban all nuclear weapons testing.
* A federal appeals court ruled that New York state education officials and the state legislature perpetuated school segregation in the city of Yonkers in the 1960's and 1970's.

* Bob Dole promised daily phone calls to talk radio stations that criticized his lack of notice to a medium that has been used extensively by President Clinton and former Republican presidential candidate Pat Buchanan.
* New York and other states began cutting food-stamp benefits to some legal immigrants under the new federal welfare law.

* Brooklyn's district attorney will be the first New York City prosecutor to seek the death penalty under the state's renewed capital punishment law, as he seeks the execution of a man charged with killing a man and chopping his body to pieces.
* A 10-million acre forestland in Ashland, Maine, and the clearcutting it has endured, is becoming a political lightning rod in this year's elections.
